method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. A script decoded each registrar, callback, jump table, vftable cell, static initializer and string literal from those bytes and asserted the addresses recorded here. Callers, stores and loads were enumerated from a linear decode of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are counts from xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json and counts from a decode of the installed client scripts into Lua 5.1 bytecode with tools/decode_lpb.py, where each CALL that follows a SELF or GETTABLE of the name was read for its argument and result counts. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the overloads that a host still had to stub: the GroupBase overload of _getProperty, the CutScene overload of _setFilename, the ActorBase _setLoopInterval store, the WidgetBase list natives _setListProperty and _updateList with the SqwtXmlDataMaker control that they drive, the argument and result handling of _callSuperClassFunction and the test of the cursor-one branch of _setTargetCursorImage. Each row gives the registration site, the declared lists, the Lua pushes of every branch, the client state that the callback reads or writes, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish group sheet content, cut scene content, list content, widget layout or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

groupKindRecord.scope: The per-kind record that GroupBase _getProperty reads, the sheet that fills it and the lookup that finds it.

facts.claim: The record of a group kind is a value in an ordered map keyed by the group kind. The key is the dword at group data +0x04, where the group data pointer sits at the receiver +0x68. 0x006BFD20 returns that dword. 0x006C2140 searches the map at ([[M]+4])+8 through the tree search 0x006D03C0 and returns the address of the node value at node +0x10. M is the dword at Y +0xE4, with Y the dword at +0x04 of the dword at the result of 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04. A key that is not in the map reaches the invalid parameter route 0x009D22B4. Whether that route returns depends on a run-time handler that the target cursor record leaves unknown, and only if it returns does the routine return the address at the end node +0x10.

The loader 0x006C9CF0 fills the map from the sheet named by the literal _group at 0x00FD4018. Its object holds a provider pointer at +0x00, a high water key at +0x04 and the map at +0x08. The provider returns the sheet by name through vtable slot 1. The loader walks the key ranges that the sheet reports through slot 14 and, for every key above the high water key, reads the row through 0x0078E220, copies the record by value (0x80 bytes) and inserts the pair of key and record through 0x006D9B20. A missing row ends the load early. After the last range it releases the sheet through provider slot 4 and stores zero at +0x00 and -1 at +0x04, so later calls return at once. It is called from 0x006CDF20 at 0x006CDF49, and the only direct caller of 0x006CDF20 is 0x00578A00. The tracked corpus inventory lists 38 rows for the decoded _group table.

The loader reads these row columns into the record. The reader 0x0078E320 returns a dword, 0x0078E280 a byte and 0x0078E360 a Utf8String. Column 0 goes to +0x00. Columns 0x10 through 0x13 go to the dwords at +0x04, +0x08, +0x0C and +0x10. Columns 0x18 through 0x1B go to the four words of a word vector at +0x18. Column 6 and column 7 go to the bytes at +0x24 and +0x25, read as dwords with the low byte kept. Column 1 goes to the byte at +0x26. Columns 0x14 through 0x17 go to the bytes at +0x27 through +0x2A. Column 3 goes to the string at +0x2C, built by 0x0044AB90 as the literal /Group/ at 0x00FD4024 followed by the column 3 text.

For the columns that GroupBase _getProperty exposes, the selector equals the sheet column. The callback reads selector 0 and the selectors 0x10 through 0x13 as dwords, selectors 6 and 7 as bytes pushed as ints, selector 1 and selectors 0x14 through 0x17 as bytes pushed as bools and selector 3 as a string. Columns 0x18 through 0x1B are the word vector, which the callback does not read. The helper 0x006E21D0 indexes that vector and returns one word, and no code or data reference to it was found.

Column 3 with the /Group/ prefix has the shape of a Lua script path. The literal /Group/GroupBaseClass at 0x00FE0EBC uses the same prefix. The string is read as the script class path of the group kind and selector 3 as its last path component. No shipped script calls selector 3.

Selector 3 is built by 0x006BF830 from the record string at +0x2C. It copies the string, finds the last / with the reverse search 0x004466E0 through the thunk 0x00446F80 and takes the substring from the index after it through 0x00447A80. The record string always starts with /, so the result is the text after the last / of the record string.

sqwtXmlDataMaker.scope: The Sqwt control whose properties the list natives write. The class is Sqwt::Data::SqwtXmlDataMaker and the property vocabulary of the natives equals its declared properties.

constructor.note: The constructor stores the vftable cells 0x0106C904 at +0x00 and 0x0106C8F8 at +0x24 and registers the property changed callback 0x00943A00 for all eleven properties below. The class name literal SqwtXmlDataMaker is at 0x0106C7AC. The last field the code touches is at +0x20C.

propertyFacts.claim: The typed int setter 0x00926E80 that the control uses for its own writes compares the new value with the stored one, stores it and notifies the callback only when they differ, and refuses the write for a property whose bound flag is set without the caller's override. The string route of the property engine that the natives use ends in the same callback and was not read for the equal value case.

The eleven static initializers at 0x00F23400 through 0x00F23570 name each descriptor from its literal and store the property index at descriptor +0x14. Count, StringValue and FilteredCount also store a flag dword at descriptor +0x18 (0x80, 0x500 and 0x80). The constructor registers each descriptor with the callback 0x00943A00. The int properties start at -1, -1, 0, 0, 0 and -1 for SortedIndex, Index, IntValue, Count, FilteredCount and FilteredIndex, and the string properties start as null pointers that read as the empty text. The value offsets follow the constructor field stores and the typed setters 0x00942AE0 (SortedIndex +0xC4), 0x00942B10 (Index +0xCC), 0x00942BA0 (FilteredIndex +0x114) and 0x00942C70 (Action +0xFC).

That the control the natives reach by name is a SqwtXmlDataMaker follows from the exact match of the six property names that the natives write (Index, AttributeName, ValueType, IntValue, StringValue, Action) with the declared properties of this class and from the Action vocabulary. The natives address the control by a name string, and the form markup that declares the name was not read.

propertyChanged.dispatch: The callback reads the property index at [[arg+0x70]+0x14] and jumps through the 11 entry dword table at 0x00943FA8. The table holds 0x00943AD7, 0x00943AFA, 0x00943F8C, 0x00943F8C, 0x00943B81, 0x00943F8C, 0x00943F8C, 0x00943B8D, 0x00943A55, 0x00943F8C and 0x00943AA5 in property index order.

cases.behavior: Maps the sorted position at +0xC4 to a row index with 0x00943500 and writes the result to Index through 0x00942B10.

Resolves the row for Index with 0x00944850 (see rowEnsure) and stores a pointer to the row element, or zero, at +0x200. With a row it refreshes the read back with 0x00942FC0, Count with 0x00944760, SortedIndex through 0x00942CA0 and FilteredIndex through 0x009432C0. Without a row it writes Index -1 and SortedIndex -1.
Compares the Action text with the vocabulary of actions and runs the matching handler.
Rebuilds the filtered view with 0x00943580. With a document and an empty sort key it first calls virtual slot 4 of a dynamic cast of the document node, whose role was not traced.
Maps the filtered position at +0x114 to a row index with 0x00943210 and writes the result to Index through 0x00942B10.

propertyChanged.tierOfRoles: STATIC for the jump table, the targets and the calls named. INFERRED for the roles of the sorted and filtered helpers, whose bodies were not read beyond the property they write.

readBack.claim: The read back clears the current row at +0x200 and, for an Index of 0 or more below the row count, stores the row element cast to DOM_Element there. When AttributeName is not empty, the row exists and the element answers true to its slot 1 test, it reads the attribute text through element slot 7, stores the text in StringValue through 0x00942C40 and stores its integer parse through 0x00988A30 and 0x00942B40 in IntValue. Otherwise it writes the empty text to StringValue and 0 to IntValue.

actions.note: Action values are compared as exact text with repe cmpsb against the literal and its terminator. RemoveRange is compared as an 11 byte prefix through a string compare. Every native writes Action last, after Index, AttributeName, ValueType and the value property.

vocabulary.behavior: 0x00943980 recounts the rows with 0x00944760, rebuilds the filtered view with 0x00943580 and sets SortedIndex to -1 by a direct store that marks the property changed. It then runs 0x00982DA0 and stores a pointer derived from the object at +0x44 at +0x208, which were not traced.
Writes the Action text RemoveRange(0-) through 0x00942C70, which dispatches again.

Finds ( and - in the Action text, parses the integers after them and calls 0x00942DB0 with the start and end. An absent end number is read as the last row because Clear maps to RemoveRange(0-) (INFERRED).
Calls slot 3 of the row element with the StringValue text, or the empty text. No refresh follows.

Writes the attribute named by AttributeName on the row at Index. ValueType Int stores IntValue through 0x00944DA0 and ValueType String stores StringValue through 0x00944ED0. Any other ValueType writes nothing. The read back 0x00942FC0 follows in every case.
Removes the attribute named by AttributeName from the row with 0x00942540, then runs the read back.
Removes the row with 0x00943370 and refreshes Count with 0x00944760.

Allocates a 0xF4 byte row element, constructs it with 0x0099AB40 and passes it with the current row to 0x00DC33A0 on the document, then runs the read back. That the new row goes before the current row is INFERRED.

actions.reset: Every path of the dispatcher ends at 0x00943F7C, which writes the empty text to Action through 0x00942C70. Writing the same Action text twice therefore dispatches twice. An unknown Action text runs no handler and is reset the same way.

rowEnsure.claim: The row resolver takes the row index and returns a row element pointer or zero. When the document pointer at +0x204 is zero it looks one up through 0x00982A30 with the dword at +0x54 and the object at +0x3C. With no document, or an index below 0, it returns zero. Otherwise it reads the row count from the child vector that 0x00942690 returns. An index below the count returns the child cast to the element type. An index at or above the count appends one 0xF4 byte row element per missing row up to and including the index through 0x00DC34E0, names each with the text after the last / of the string that the dword at +0x54 addresses (empty when it has no /), and returns the last one created. Both paths then refresh Count through 0x00944760.

attributeStore.claim: The attribute writer takes the row element, the attribute name, the value text and one type byte. It finds the attribute by name through 0x00DC2ED0. When it exists it sets the value through slot 3. Otherwise it allocates a 0xD0 byte Sqwt::Data::XmlAttr, stores the type byte at +0xCC, sets the name and the value and appends the attribute through 0x00DC33B0. The Int writer 0x00944DA0 formats IntValue with the format %d at 0x01077268 through 0x00988A90 and passes the byte at 0x013599D1. The String writer 0x00944ED0 passes the StringValue text and the byte at 0x013599DC. Both type bytes lie beyond the file backed part of .data and are set by static initializers at run time.

filteredView.claim: With no document the view sets FilteredIndex to -1 and FilteredCount to 0. With a document and an empty FilteredSortKey the view is the unfiltered list, so FilteredIndex takes Index and FilteredCount takes Count. With a non-empty FilteredSortKey the routine walks the child rows and keeps a row whose attribute named visibility (literal 0x0106C844) is empty or any text other than False (literal 0x0106C850), orders the kept rows by 0x00945C40 with the sort key, and sets FilteredIndex from the mapped Index and FilteredCount from the kept count.

targetCursorImageBranch.scope: The cursor-one branch of DesktopWidget _setTargetCursorImage, whose test asks the work store for one member. The store, the argument handling and the image side effects are in manifests/target_cursor_native_contract.json.

facts.claim: The callback 0x006E5030 reads two ints and calls 0x0075EFC0 with the first minus 1 and the second at 0x006E50E2. When that zero-based index is not 0, or the byte at DesktopWidget +0x7C is not 0, it returns. Otherwise it builds the widget identity with 0x00CC73B0 at 0x006E5106 and calls 0x00CC7BE0 with that identity, the immediate 0x0007A124 (500004) and -1 at 0x006E5118 through 0x006E511E. The same call with the same immediate appears at 0x006FEB1F and 0x006FED56, in the DesktopWidget methods 0x006FE960 and 0x006FEBB0 that store +0x7C and fire the Lua callbacks _onTargetChanged and _onTargetDecided. The widget identity feeds only this test.

The immediate 500004 is a work key. widget/desktopwidget_connector binds it as the work member mainTargetDecidedFlag of the desktop widget with _bindWork(500004, "work", "mainTargetDecidedFlag"), next to the keys 500001 (tutorialMenuType), 500002 (tutorialFlag) and 500003 (tutorialLockFlag). The same script reads and assigns the member in five of its prototypes.

0x00CC7BE0 returns false when the 0x00CD8160 lookup of the identity is null, the record byte at +0x7D is 0 or the record dword at +0x14 is 0. Otherwise it fetches the work operator that 0x00CEB490 returns for the object at manager +0x214 and calls 0x00CE53D0 on it with the key and the index. 0x00CE53D0 finds the entry of the key through 0x00CE5040, returns false when there is none, adds the index to the entry offset only when the short at entry +0x08 is not negative and reads the member through 0x00D11C00, which splits the packed slot value into value >> 3 and value & 7 for 0x00CE45D0 and 0x00CCB4D0.
The returned byte is the boolean value of the work member, so the branch tracks whether the main target is decided. The read of the member value through 0x00CCB4D0 was not traced.

After the test the branch reads the identity of cursor 0 through 0x0075F0E0. A true result with +0x70 equal to the dword at 0x0130C778 posts the 0xCD message with that identity as both values and stores it at +0x70. A false result with +0x70 different from that dword posts the message with that identity and the dword, which holds 0xE0000000, and stores the dword at +0x70. The 0xCD message is built by 0x0075EB30 and passed to 0x004D6D10, which jumps to 0x004E0240 and from there to 0x00DAE010. That routine copies the 8 bytes at record +0x18 into the outbound packet body, the framing recorded in docs/search-recruitment-wire-contract.md, and sends a 0xCD record only while its state dword at +0x8C is 3. 0x0075D460 copies three dwords of the callback receiver chain into a local record, and 0x0075EB30 uses the first dword to reach the sender object. The methods 0x006FE960 and 0x006FEBB0 are reached from LuaActorImpl vftable slots 25 and 26 through the trampolines 0x008A3EA0 and 0x008A3ED0, and they hold +0x7C at 1 for the duration of the script callback. For cursor index 0 they set +0x70 to the identity argument when the 0x0007A124 query is true and to 0xE0000000 otherwise. manifests/target_cursor_native_contract.json records the evidence.

rows.callbackKind: direct member function of the const GroupBase holder

arguments.note: Property selector, which is the column of the group kind row. It is compared unsigned against 0x17.

rows.behavior: Finds the record of the receiver's group kind (see framework.groupKindRecord) and pushes one value chosen by the selector. Selectors 0, 6, 7 and 0x10 through 0x13 push an int, selectors 1 and 0x14 through 0x17 push a bool and selector 3 pushes a string. Every other selector, including a negative one, pushes nothing and the Lua call receives no value. The native reads client state only, writes nothing and does not yield.

branches.note: Target 0x0070051C. The byte is zero extended.
Target 0x00700522. The byte is zero extended.

pushes: string: text after the last / of record string +0x2C

branches.condition: selectors 2, 4, 5, 8 through 0xF, 0x18 and above, and negative selectors
branches.note: The byte table 0x0070065C maps them to the empty target 0x00700603.

Row of the _group sheet for the kind.

rows.evidenceTier: STATIC for the registration, selector dispatch, record layout and loader. MEASURED for the call sites. INFERRED for the roles of the columns.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x0074D940 pushes the name literal 0x00FD76B4 at 0x0074DA29, which is the literal of the WidgetBase overload as well. It loads the callback 0x00700450 into ESI at 0x0074D977 and calls the return list builder 0x007430F0, the argument list builder 0x00728C20, the const GroupBase wrapper 0x007265C0 and the installer 0x00CCCAD0. Its only caller is 0x00757C9D, the 14th registrar call of the GroupBase switchboard 0x00757B70.

The callback keeps the ExecuteParameters pointer in ESI and the receiver in EDI. It reaches M through 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04, the chain of the scheduler contracts and Y +0xE4, loads the key through 0x006BFD20 on the receiver +0x68 and calls 0x006C2140 on M. It then tests the cell vector size, which calls 0x009D22B4 when empty, reads the selector through 0x005819A0 and compares it unsigned with 0x17.

The selector reaches the targets through the 24 byte table at 0x0070065C and the dword table at 0x00700624. The byte table holds 0, 1, 13, 2, 13, 13, 3, 4, 13, 13, 13, 13, 13, 13, 13, 13, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. The dword table holds 0x007004FF, 0x007005D6, 0x00700528, 0x0070051C, 0x00700522, 0x0070056A, 0x00700585, 0x007005A0, 0x007005BB, 0x007005DB, 0x007005E0, 0x007005E5, 0x007005EA and 0x00700603 in slot order.

The int targets push through 0x00584F70, the bool targets through 0x00748870 and the string target through 0x007487C0 after 0x006BF830 builds the string into a local that 0x00446F50 then destroys. All pushes write the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.

The call-site index lists 90 sites of _getProperty, of which five are GroupBase calls in group/communitygroup/companygroup (lines 104, 119 and 210) and group/communitygroup/retainergroup (lines 19 and 33). A decode of the installed scripts shows that all five pass the selector 0. Four take exactly one result. The site at companygroup line 210 is the last argument of a _bindWorkNestingArray call and forwards every result of the call, which is the single value of this overload.

The scripts use the selector 0 value as the length of the _memberSave array in the sync declaration of the group work, as the loop bound over the members and as the array length argument of _bindWorkNestingArray. The value is therefore read as the member capacity of the group kind. The meaning of the other columns has no script reader in the shipped client.

rows.callbackKind: direct member function of the non-const CutScene holder
rows.behavior: Assigns the Utf8String to the string object at receiver +0x6C through 0x00447450 and returns. It resolves no control identity, calls no manager and starts no load. The string is read later by _play, which hands its address to the cut scene manager. A cell that is not a string reaches the mismatch routine 0x00CCA730 in the reader 0x0071CE70, which then returns the static empty string at 0x0134B4C8. No yield.

branches.note: The only effect is the string assignment.

consumers.note: Passes the address of receiver +0x6C at 0x006FB8DB to 0x0076D610 on the cut scene manager, the dword at Y +0x08. The routine copies the first 0x1F bytes of the name, or all of a shorter name, into a zeroed 0x20 byte field and posts a message with code 0xCE and size 0x38 through 0x004D6D10. The message is the serverbound 0x00CE record that manifests/cutscene_native_call_contract.json describes.
Calls the sibling 0x0076D820 on the same manager with no file name, so it does not read +0x6C.

rows.evidenceTier: STATIC for the registration, the store and the consumer calls. MEASURED for the call site. INFERRED for the string extent.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x00735EB0 loads the callback 0x006E7A60 into ESI at 0x00735EE7, calls the return list builder 0x0072B440, the argument list builder 0x0072B5B0 (one Utf8String) and the non-const CutScene wrapper 0x00726880, pushes the shared literal 0x00FD6D90 at 0x00735F99 and installs through 0x00CCCAD0. Its only caller is 0x007547EC, the first registrar call of the CutScene switchboard 0x007547D0.

The callback reads the cell vector size with the 0x009D22B4 failure route, reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 and assigns the result to the string at ECX +0x6C through 0x00447450 at 0x006E7A9B. ECX is the CutScene receiver. The WidgetBase overload instead resolves the control identity at ExecuteParameters +0x0C through 0x004D9910, and the SpreadSheet overload calls a manager virtual slot, so the CutScene overload is the one with no manager call.

The string object is 0x54 bytes by the layout that its constructors write (a 0x40 byte inline buffer at +0x12), so the name spans +0x6C through +0xBF. The byte at +0xC1 is the skip flag that _skip sets and _play and _replay clear, and the CutScene object is 0xC4 bytes in the create actor record.

0x0076D610 builds the message: it zeroes a 0x20 byte field, copies the lesser of the name length and 0x1F bytes into it through 0x009D4600, fills a record with code 0xCE and size 0x38 and posts it through 0x004D6D10 on the first dword of the manager. The two argument vectors go through 0x00784840 and 0x007848E0 first.

The call-site index lists three _setFilename sites, one per overload. The CutScene site is gamedata/cutscene line 35, in CutScene._onInit. It passes the first _onInit parameter as the only argument and takes no result. The other sites are gamedata/spreadsheet line 11 and widget/widgetbaseclass line 193.

rows.callbackKind: thunk to 0x0078C020 that adds the receiver
rows.behavior: Appends up to five 16 bit values to the word vector of the receiver's control record. An argument 0 of Nil appends the one word 0x7FFF and stops. Otherwise it appends one word per leading non-Nil float, in argument order, and stops at the first Nil. Each word is the low 16 bits of trunc(trunc(f * 10000.0 + 0.5) / 10), with both truncations toward zero, which is f seconds in milliseconds for values that fit. The native never clears the vector, so repeated calls accumulate. No yield and no Lua result.

branches.note: One call to 0x00CC7400 with the static word at 0x0130CF00, whose file image holds 0x7FFF. The static has only read references.
Loop over the five declared cells at 0x0078C090 through 0x0078C15B. A Nil cell ends it at 0x0078C0BA.

rows.evidenceTier: STATIC for the registration, the conversion and the store. MEASURED for the call sites. INFERRED for the role of the vector.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x00742760 loads the thunk 0x006DBD90 into ESI at 0x00742797, calls the return list builder 0x0072B440, the argument list builder 0x00741CD0 (five floats), the const ActorBase wrapper 0x00726300, pushes the literal 0x00FD75E8 at 0x00742849 and installs through 0x00CCCAD0. Its only caller is 0x00753C8B, the fourth registrar call of the ActorBase switchboard 0x00753C30. The thunk calls 0x0078C020 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and the receiver.

0x0078C020 tests the tag of cell 0 against 6 (Nil) at 0x0078C068. For Nil it calls 0x00CC7400 with the receiver and the address 0x0130CF00 and returns. Otherwise it loops over the five 16 byte cells. A Nil cell ends the loop. A float cell goes through the float reader 0x0071BAC0, is promoted to a double, multiplied by 10000.0 (0x00FE0570) and increased by 0.5 (0x00F59898), truncated by cvttsd2si, divided by 10 with the signed multiply by 0x66666667, wrapped by 0x00CD6AB0 (which stores the low word of its argument) and passed to 0x00CC7400 with the receiver.

0x00CC7400 takes the manager from the first dword of the engine context, resolves the receiver's record through 0x00CD7A30 and calls 0x00CE2E40 on it. 0x00CD7A30 returns the record at control +0x04, or the root record at manager +0x1BC when the control is the root control. 0x00CE2E40 reserves 8 words at record +0x20 when the vector has no capacity and then appends the word through 0x00CE3EE0.

The raw Lua function that the engine bootstrap registers as __lge_setLoopInterval at 0x00D083B0 appends to the same vector through 0x00CE2E40 for the Lua arguments 2 through the top. It converts each Lua number to an integer with 0x009D6600, appends the static word at 0x0130CF00 when the integer equals the static word masked with 0x7FFF and appends a wrapped word otherwise. It applies no seconds conversion, so the word 0x7FFF is a distinguished value on both routes.

The vector holds the loop intervals of the control. Six of the seven script sites are in scripts that define _onLoop themselves (AreaBaseClass, MapObjFireworks, InstanceRaidBaseClass, DesktopWidget, WidgetBaseClass and DebugBaseClass), and the bootstrap installs an _onLoop metatable. The consumer that reads the vector and calls _onLoop was not traced.

The call-site index lists seven sites. Six pass one explicit value and DebugBaseClass.setLoopInterval forwards its varargs. The constants are 1 in AreaBaseClass, InstanceRaidBaseClass, DesktopWidget and CommandDebuggerDEV, 10 in MapObjFireworks and 0.1 in WidgetBaseClass. No site uses a result.

rows.callbackKind: direct member function that forwards to the typed branch routines

arguments.note: Name of the list control, the SqwtXmlDataMaker, within the receiver's widget.
Row index. Written as the Index property.
Attribute name. Written as the AttributeName property.
Attribute value. Tag 0 int, tag 2 bool, tag 3 Utf8String. Any other tag, the float tag 1 and Nil included, writes nothing.

rows.behavior: Sets one attribute of one row of a list control by writing five properties of the control in order and then the Action property. The properties are Index (the row), AttributeName, ValueType, IntValue or StringValue, and Action with the text SetAttr. The control creates the missing rows up to Index when Index is written, stores the attribute on the row when Action is written and resets Action. An int value is written with ValueType Int and IntValue, stored as its %d text. A string value is written with ValueType String and StringValue. A bool is written with ValueType String and the StringValue text True or False. The native yields nothing and returns nothing. A list name that no control answers to, or a control with no document, ends the writes without an error.

writes: StringValue = True (0x0134B790) for a nonzero byte or False (0x0134B7E8) for zero

branches.note: Branch routine 0x006EAA20, which the sibling _setListTextProperty also uses with a composed string.

branches.condition: value tag 1 (float) or any other tag

facts.claim: The registrar 0x00744460 loads the callback 0x006F3E70 into ESI at 0x00744497 and calls the return list builder 0x0072B440, the argument list builder 0x00744170, the wrapper 0x00726A90 and the installer 0x00CCCAD0, with the literal 0x00FD76A0 pushed at 0x00744549. Its only caller is 0x00754BCC, the 17th registrar call of the WidgetBase switchboard 0x00754A60. The argument list builder makes Utf8String, int, Utf8String (through 0x00742CB0 position 2) and the composite of 0x00740A20, which 0x0073E330 fills with Utf8String, int and bool.

The callback copies the dwords at ExecuteParameters +0x04 (the engine context), +0x10 (the argument cell holder) and +0x0C (the control identity) into a three dword local record and calls 0x0072B210 on the cell holder with the cell index 3 and the record. It does not read an argument itself.

0x0072B210 tests the cell vector size against the index with the 0x009D22B4 failure route, then reads the tag byte at cell +0x0C and the value pointer at cell +0x08. Tag 0 calls 0x006EA360 with the int, tag 2 calls 0x006EA6D0 with the byte and tag 3 calls 0x006EAA20 with the string pointer. Tag 1 and every other tag return with no call.

Each branch routine reads argument 0 through 0x0071CE70, argument 1 through 0x005819A0 and argument 2 through 0x0071CE70, copies the two strings, resolves the engine from the identity with 0x0075BB60 (which calls 0x004D9910) and makes five calls to 0x0075BB80. Each call passes the list name, a property name string built by 0x00447260 and a pickup. The pickups are an int pickup from 0x00716950 for Index and IntValue, a string pickup from 0x00716AC0 for AttributeName and the string value and the static pickups below for ValueType, the bool text and Action.

The static pickups are built by static initializers from literals. 0x0134B790 holds True (0x00FD4D6C) from 0x00F17FF0, 0x0134B7E8 holds False (0x00FD4D74) from 0x00F18070, 0x0134B840 holds Int (0x00FD4D7C) from 0x00F180F0, 0x0134B898 holds String (0x00FD4D80) from 0x00F18170 and 0x0134B8F0 holds SetAttr (0x00FD4D88) from 0x00F181F0. The sibling pickups 0x0134B948 (InsertIndex), 0x0134B9A0 (RemoveIndex), 0x0134B9F8 (RemoveRange(0-)) and 0x0134BA50 (Update) come from 0x00F18270, 0x00F182F0, 0x00F18370 and 0x00F183F0.

0x0075BB80 jumps to 0x005355A0, which calls 0x005354D0 with the empty string at 0x01266B10 as the context. An empty context selects the default index at engine +0x98, and a non-empty context would be resolved by 0x005353E0 with a negative result ending the call. 0x005354D0 then builds the property processor with 0x0053BC30 from the engine, the index, the list name and the property name and invokes slot 1 of the pickup with it. The processor formats an int as %d, converts a bool to True or False and forwards a string, then reaches the property engine, which ends the write when it resolves no control for the name, as the widget item record gives.

The writes land on a SqwtXmlDataMaker, as framework.sqwtXmlDataMaker lists: Index creates the rows and selects the row, AttributeName reads the attribute back, ValueType, IntValue and StringValue only store their value, and Action SetAttr stores the attribute and resets Action.

The order of the five writes decides the result, because Index must create and select the row before Action stores into it. The pickup is invoked synchronously with the processor, as the visibility property path record gives. That the property engine entry 0x00912850 then runs the control's property changed callback during each write, so that the callbacks run in write order, was not read in the engine itself.

The call-site index lists 62 sites. 58 are in widget/retaineritemlistwidget, 3 in widget/aetherytelistwidget and 1 in the widget/widgetbaseclass_common wrapper setListProperty. All 62 pass four explicit arguments and use no result. The wrapper setListProperty has 853 call sites in 46 scripts, 817 with four explicit arguments and 36 that forward varargs, so most widget lists reach this native through the wrapper. The retaineritemlistwidget sites pass string values such as Collapsed and numbers such as an icon id or a stack count. AetheryteListWidget.addListItem writes AetheryteID and Cost as numbers and CostVisibility as the bool false to the list ListBox, which exercises the bool branch. AetheryteListWidget.createRegionList writes the rows 0 through 4 of RegionList through the wrapper with the attribute RegionID and no row insertion, then calls _updateList on RegionList.
How the declared Which<Utf8String,int,bool> reader treats a Lua number with a fractional part was not traced. The cell tag set by that reader decides between the int branch and the no-op for tag 1.

rows.behavior: Writes the Action property of the named list control with the text Update. The control recounts its rows and rebuilds its filtered view. The native writes no Index, AttributeName or value property and returns nothing. A list name that no control answers to ends the write without an error. No yield.
rows.evidenceTier: STATIC for the registration, the write and the control handler. MEASURED for the call sites. INFERRED for the redraw of a bound list box.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x00738F40 loads the thunk 0x006EBE60 into ESI at 0x00738F77 and calls the return list builder 0x0072B440, the argument list builder 0x0072B5B0 (one Utf8String), the wrapper 0x00726A90 and the installer 0x00CCCAD0, with the literal 0x00FD7008 pushed at 0x00739029. Its only caller is 0x00754C35, the 22nd registrar call of the WidgetBase switchboard 0x00754A60. The thunk passes ExecuteParameters +0x04, +0x10 and the address of +0x0C to 0x006EB450.

0x006EB450 reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70, builds the property name Action from the literal 0x00FD4D60 and calls 0x0075B810 with the control identity, the list name, the property name and the static pickup 0x0134BA50. 0x0075B810 resolves the engine with 0x004D9910 and calls 0x005355A0, the same route as the five writes of _setListProperty.

The Action text Update reaches the handler 0x00943980 of the control. It recounts the rows with 0x00944760, rebuilds the filtered view with 0x00943580 and sets SortedIndex to -1. With an empty FilteredSortKey the filtered view equals the full list. The handler can change the Count and FilteredCount properties, whose change notifications are the only redraw signal found.
A list box or other consumer bound to the data maker redraws from the property change notifications of Count, FilteredCount and FilteredIndex. The binding and the redraw path were not traced.

The call-site index lists 13 sites. 10 are in widget/retaineritemlistwidget, 2 in widget/aetherytelistwidget and 1 in the widget/widgetbaseclass_common wrapper updateListProperty. All 13 pass one argument and use no result. The wrapper updateListProperty has 202 call sites in 42 scripts, 196 with one argument and 6 that forward varargs.

arguments.note: The whole present suffix of the Lua arguments, one cell per value.

rows.behavior: Calls the method of the class above the running method's class with the method name and with every trailing value of the Lua call, and pushes every result of that call. The declared list holds one Variable after the name, and that entry consumes all present trailing values of a recognized kind (nil, boolean, number, string and control table), so the number of trailing values has no fixed limit. A trailing value of another kind ends the scan and the call raises the GetArguments_ diagnostic. With no trailing value the marshaller supplies one Nil cell in its place. The number of results is whatever the super method returns.
rows.yieldsNote: The callback itself does not yield. The super method runs on the same Lua thread and can yield there.
rows.evidenceTier: STATIC for the registration, the copy and the result loop. MEASURED for the call-site shapes. INFERRED for the append of the whole suffix and for the Nil placeholder reaching the super method.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x0072DF60 loads the thunk 0x006DBC40 into ESI at 0x0072DF97 and calls the return list builder 0x00728AC0, the argument list builder 0x0072B290, the const ActorBase wrapper 0x00726300 and the installer 0x00CCCAD0, with the literal 0x00FD65D4 pushed at 0x0072E049. Its only caller is 0x00753C4C, the first registrar call of the ActorBase switchboard 0x00753C30. The thunk calls 0x0078D520 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and the receiver at 0x006DBC7F.

0x0078D520 reads cell 0 as the method name through 0x0071CE70, copies the cells from index 1 to the end of the cell vector into a local container through 0x00753B90 with the start index pushed as 1, converts the container through 0x00791030 and calls 0x00CD25F0 with the thread context at ExecuteParameters +0x08, the name and the converted list. It then walks the result cells in order and pushes each by its tag into the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.
0x00753B90 loops from cell start index to the end of the vector and appends each cell to the destination through 0x00584EE0, so the copy has no count limit.

The widget contract record framework.variableArgumentReader gives the Variable reader no fixed limit: a recognized suffix of T-p+1 present positions is consumed and the cursor returns to T+1, with an unsupported tag left unconsumed so that the GetArguments_ bound check fails. Read with the copy above, the declared list of one Variable does not bound the trailing values to one. This is the reconciliation of the arity conflict that the widget record leaves open. The door record reads the super call with the name _onInit and trailing A2 and A3 as preserving both values, and the marshaller admits them.

The recognized raw tags 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 are read as the Lua type codes of nil, boolean, number, string and table, with the table accepted only when it resolves to a control. Raw tag 3 chooses an int or a float cell through 0x00CF3670, whose rule is untraced. A function, userdata or other table ends the scan.

When the call passes no trailing value the Variable position is past the Lua top. The dispatcher fallback of the marshaller then appends one tag 6 (Nil) cell without reading a Lua value, which the copy at index 1 includes. That the super method receives this cell as one explicit nil argument was not traced past the conversion 0x00791030, whose tag 6 branch appends it to the converted container through 0x00748D10.

The call-site index lists 84 sites of the name. A decode of the installed scripts counts them by argument shape: 44 pass the method name only, 11 pass one trailing value, 19 pass two, 2 pass three, 2 pass four and 6 forward varargs. No site uses a result.

obligations: Hold a table of group kind rows keyed by the group kind that the group data carries, filled from the _group sheet with the columns of framework.groupKindRecord.
Read the selector as an int and push nothing for a selector outside 0, 1, 3, 6, 7 and 0x10 through 0x17.
Push selectors 0, 6, 7 and 0x10 through 0x13 as ints, selectors 1 and 0x14 through 0x17 as bools and selector 3 as the text after the last / of /Group/ followed by the column 3 text.
Treat a kind with no row as a client failure. Retail reaches the invalid parameter route 0x009D22B4, whose outcome is unknown (CALIBRATION for any recovery).
Store the Utf8String on the CutScene object and return. Start no load and call no manager.
Hand the stored name to _play and not to _replay. _play copies at most 31 bytes of it into the message that the cut scene manager receives.
Append one 16 bit word to the control's loop interval list for each leading non-Nil float, up to five, in order, as the low 16 bits of trunc(trunc(f * 10000.0 + 0.5) / 10).
Append the single word 0x7FFF when argument 0 is Nil and stop at the first Nil otherwise.
Never clear the list in this native. The consumer that fires _onLoop from the list is open.
Keep a named list per widget with rows, each a map from attribute name to text, and address it by the list name of argument 0. Ignore a name that no list answers to without an error.

On _setListProperty write Index, AttributeName, ValueType, the value property and then Action in that order, as the properties of the list. Index must grow the row list to Index + 1 rows when it is at or above the row count and must clear the current row when it is negative or the list has no document.

On the Action SetAttr, store the attribute only when a current row exists. ValueType Int stores the %d text of IntValue and ValueType String stores the StringValue text. Any other ValueType stores nothing. Then reset Action to the empty text.
Write an int as ValueType Int, a string as ValueType String and a bool as ValueType String with the text True or False. Write nothing for any other value kind.
On _updateList write Action Update, which recounts the rows and recomputes the filtered view. Notify the bound consumers of the changed Count and FilteredCount (INFERRED, binding untraced).
Keep rows whose visibility attribute is the text False out of the filtered view only when FilteredSortKey is not empty.

Run the Index handler only when the Index value changes, since the typed property setters notify only on a changed value. A repeat write of the same Index does not resolve the row again (INFERRED for the string route of the property engine).
Run the branch only for the first cursor with DesktopWidget +0x7C clear, after the image store of the target cursor record.

Read the desktop widget work member mainTargetDecidedFlag (key 500004) as the test. With it true and no cached identity, cache the identity of cursor 0 and post the 0xCD message with that identity as both values. With it false and a cached identity, post the message with the identity of cursor 0 and the no identity value, and clear the cache to the no identity value.

Write +0x70 from the target changed and target decided events: for index 0 after the script callback, and for any index when the cursor count is below index plus 1. Hold +0x7C at 1 while their script callbacks run.
Pass every trailing Lua value of a recognized kind to the super method and raise the argument diagnostic at the first value of another kind.
Push every result of the super method, with no fixed count.
Resolve the class above the running method's class with the call frame rule of the door initialization record.

ledgerCandidates.note: This record gives the GroupBase _getProperty overload a body once a host holds the _group sheet rows, the CutScene _setFilename overload a body that stores the name, _setLoopInterval a body that appends the converted words, _setListProperty and _updateList a body over a row and attribute model that follows framework.sqwtXmlDataMaker, and _callSuperClassFunc a lifted arity. The open questions name the inputs that stay CALIBRATION. The cursor-one branch of _setTargetCursorImage now has the identity of its test, the work member mainTargetDecidedFlag, and still lacks the consumers of the posted message. A host that implements the list natives needs the data maker names that the form markup declares, which this record does not read.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: Which _group rows and column values do the CompanyGroup and RetainerGroup kinds carry?
openQuestions.constraint: GroupBase _getProperty returns sheet column values. The tracked corpus inventory counts 38 rows for the _group table and no tracked artifact promotes a row value. The five script sites read selector 0 only.
openQuestions.needs: A decode of the _group sheet from the installed client under the retail-input validation procedure, with the group kinds that CompanyGroup and RetainerGroup receive at creation.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: What reads the word vector at group record +0x18 (columns 0x18 through 0x1B)?
openQuestions.constraint: The helper 0x006E21D0 returns one word of the vector and no code or data reference to it was found. GroupBase _getProperty does not read the vector.
openQuestions.needs: A trace of the callers of the helper through indirect calls or a live run that records the group natives a script calls.

openQuestions.question: How does the server resolve the cut scene file name that the serverbound 0x00CE record carries?
openQuestions.constraint: _play sends the name in a 0x20 byte field of the serverbound 0x00CE record, as manifests/cutscene_native_call_contract.json records. The server side consumer and the path rule are outside the client.
openQuestions.needs: A retail capture that pairs the 0x00CE record with the server reply sequence.

openQuestions.constraint: The vector is written only by the append 0x00CE2E40. The unit and the use of the second to fifth word are open, and the 0x7FFF word is a distinguished value of both writers.
openQuestions.needs: A trace of the readers of record +0x24 and +0x28 in the Lua control record code and the _onLoop firer.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: Which routines call LuaActorImpl vftable slots 25 and 26, which reach the DesktopWidget methods that write +0x7C, and what index and identity do they pass?
openQuestions.constraint: The 0xCD message path, the effect of 0x0075D460 and the methods writing +0x7C are traced in manifests/target_cursor_native_contract.json. The virtual callers of the two slots are untraced, and so is whether the work member holds a value before any script assigns it.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: Does a super call with no trailing value deliver one explicit nil to the super method?
openQuestions.constraint: The marshaller appends a Nil cell for the omitted Variable position and the copy includes it. Whether the call preparation pushes it was not traced past the argument conversion.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Callers, stores and loads come from a linear decode of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. An absent reference is not proof that none exists.
The MEASURED script facts come from a decode of the installed client scripts and the chunk bodies and the scan are not tracked. The counts of the shipped call-site index agree with them.
The SqwtXmlDataMaker identification of the list control rests on the property vocabulary and the constructor registration. The form markup that names the control was not read.
Group sheet values, cut scene content, list content and loop timing are data or consumers that this record does not establish.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish widget layout, redraw or server behavior.
